pages.text: "Finished playing!" Pipo left his wooden ball rolling and dropped the shovel in the yard, then ran home. Sheep entered the pen; the gate closed. Bedtime. Picking up the ball and shovel was what he disliked most.
"I will play again tomorrow morning!" He slipped under the covers. Outside the round window, it was dark. Then patter, patter—rain hit the glass.
Morning. Sheep called baa at the gate. Pipo ran outside. "My ball! My shovel!" The ball was soaked; the shovel half buried in mud.
"Waaah, my ball is wet!" His eyes grew damp. Mom came out. "Pipo, why so sad?" Looking around, she smiled. "I will teach you some magic."
Mom opened the shed wide. "Look. Left in the yard, things get rain, mud, and a whole night of soaking. But in the shed—" Her basket on the shelf was perfectly dry.
Mom sang, "Used it? Put it back! Dry, even in rain!" She tapped the shelf, then the wall peg. "Ball here, shovel here." Pipo repeated, "Used it? Put it back!"
Pipo wiped the wet ball with hay and put it on the shelf. He shook mud from the shovel and hung it on the peg. "Ball here, shovel here. Used it? Put it back!"
At evening, sheep entered and the gate closed. Pipo crouched by the shed, hands at his chest. "My ball is in the shed!" Putting out the yard lamp, Mom smiled. "No worries today, right?"
Morning: it had rained all night, but the ball on the shelf was dry! Now Pipo did three things after play. "One, finish and pick up! Two, into their places! Three, shed door shut!"
Pipo hugged Mom's legs. "I put your basket on the shelf too!" Putting things back after use made tomorrow's play dry too. Hugging his dry ball, he smiled. "Used it? Put it back!"
